questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A light ray of wavelength 546 nm is incident on an air-glass interface. If the speed of light in air is $3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$. Then, wavelength of light ray in glass will be
[Take, refractive index of glass, $\mu=1.5$ ]
questions.solution:
Given, wavelength of light,
$\lambda=546 \mathrm{ nm}
Refractive ve index, $\mu=1.5$
Speed of light, $c=3 \times 10^6 $\mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$
Refractive index,
$\begin{aligned} \mu & =\frac{\text{ Speed$ of $light in vacuum (c) }}{\text{ Speed of light in glass (v) }} \\ & =\frac{c}{v} \\ & =\frac{v \lambda}{v \lambda_g}\left[\lambda_g=\text{ wavelength of light in glass }\right] \\ \mu & =\frac{\lambda}{\lambda_g} \Rightarrow \lambda_g=\frac{\lambda}{\mu} \\ & =\frac{546}{1.5}=364 \mathrm{ nm}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: When the ray suffers minimum deviation, it becomes parallel to the base of prism P. As prisms $\mathrm{Q}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are of same material and have identical shape, therefore, the ray continues to be parallel to base of $Q$ and $R$. Hence final deviation of the ray remains the same as before.

questions.q: A compound microscope having magnifying power 35 with its eye-piece of focal length 10 $\mathrm{cm}$. Assume that the final image is at least distance of distinct vision then the magnification produced by the objective is
questions.solution: For a compound microscope, magnifying power $\mathrm{MP}=\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}} \times \mathrm{m}_{0}$ When the final image is at least distance of distance vision then $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{e}}=1+\frac{\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{e}}} \\ \therefore \quad & \mathrm{MP}=\mathrm{m}_{0}\left[1+\frac{\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{e}}}\right] \\ \Rightarrow \quad &-35=\mathrm{m}_{0}\left[1+\frac{25}{10}\right] \\ \Rightarrow \quad &-35=\mathrm{m}_{0} \times 35 \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \mathrm{m}_{0}=-10 \end{aligned}$ The negative sign shows that the image formed by objective is inverted.

questions.q: The refractive index for a prism is given as $\mu=\cot \frac{A}{2}$. Then, angle of minimum deviation in terms of angle of prism is
questions.solution: Using prism formula, $\mu=\frac{\sin \left(\frac{\mathrm{A}+\delta_{\mathrm{m}}}{2}\right)}{\sin \left(\frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)}$ ...(i) where, $A=$ angle of prism $\delta_{\mathrm{m}}=$ angle of minimum deviation Given, $\mu=\cot \left(\frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)=\frac{\cos \left(\frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)}{\sin \left(\frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)}$ So, from Eq. (i) $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\cos \left(\frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)}{\sin \left(\frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)}=\frac{\sin \left(\frac{\mathrm{A}+\delta_{\mathrm{m}}}{2}\right)}{\sin \left(\frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)} \\ \Rightarrow & \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)=\sin \left(\frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}+\frac{\delta_{\mathrm{m}}}{2}\right) \\ \Rightarrow & \delta_{\mathrm{m}}=\pi-2 \mathrm{ A}=180^{{}^{\circ}}-2 \mathrm{ A} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two convex lenses of power $2 \mathrm{D}$ and $5 \mathrm{D}$ are separated by a distance $\frac{1}{3} \mathrm{ m}$. The power of optical system formed is
questions.solution: Given: $\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{P}_{1}=$2 $\mathrm{D}$ ; $\mathrm{P}_{2}=3 \mathrm{D} \\ \mathrm{d}$=$\frac{1}{3} \mathrm{ m}$ \end{array}$ We know that \frac{1}{\mathrm{ F}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{1}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{2}}-\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{f}_{1} \cdot \mathrm{f}_{2}} Equivatent power, \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad$& P=P_{1}+P_{2}-d P_{1} $\cdot$ P_{2} \\ &=2+3-$\frac{1}{3} \times2 \times3=3 D \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A students plots a graph between inverse of magnification $1 / m$ produced by a convex thin lens and the object distance $u$ as shown in figure. What was the focal length of the lens used?
questions.solution:
Lens formula, $\frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}$
or $\frac{\mathrm{u}}{\mathrm{v}}-1=\frac{\mathrm{u}}{\mathrm{f}}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{ m}}-1=\frac{\mathrm{u}}{\mathrm{f}}$ or $\frac{1}{\mathrm{ m}}=\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}\right) \mathrm{u}+1$
this is the equation of a straight line whose slope
$\frac{1}{f}-\frac{b}{c} \therefore 1-\frac{c}{b}$

questions.q: A small coil is introduced between the poles of an electromagnet so that its axis coincides with the magnetic field direction. The number of turns is $n$ and the cross-sectional area of the coil is $A$. When the coil turns through $180^{{}^{\circ}}$ about its diameter, the charge flowing through the coil is Q. The total resistance of the circuit is $R$. What is the magnitude of the magnetic induction?
questions.solution:
Induced charge

$\begin{aligned}$ Q &$=-\frac{n B A}{R} \left(\cos \theta_{2}-\cos \theta_{1}\right)$\\
&$$=-\frac{n B A}{R}\left(\cos$$180^{{}^{\circ}}-$\cos 0^{{}^{\circ}}\right$) \\
\Rightarrow B & =$\frac{Q R}{2 n A}$
\end{aligned}$$

questions.q:
Four light sources produce the following four waves:
(i) $ y_{1}=a \sin   \left(\omegat+\phi_{1}\right)
(ii) $y_{2}=a \sin 2 \omegat$
(iii) $y_{3}=a \sin  $\left(\omegat+\phi_{2}\right)$
(iv) $y_{4}=a \sin (3 \omegat+\phi)$
Superposition of which two waves give rise to interference?
questions.solution:
Inteference takes place between two waves having equal frequency and propagate in same direction.
Hence, $y_{1}=a \sin  \left(\omegat+\phi_{1}\right)$ y_{3}=a^{\prime} \sin $\left(\omegat+\phi_{2}\right) same frequency \omega.$

questions.q: A ray PQ incident on the refracting face BA is refracted in the prism BAC as shown in the figure and emerges from the other refracting face $\mathrm{AC}$ as $\mathrm{RS}$ such that $\mathrm{AQ}=\mathrm{AR}$. If the angle of prism $\mathrm{A}=60^{{}^{\circ}}$ and the refractive index of the material of prism is $\sqrt{3}, then the angle of deviation of the ray is $
questions.solution: Given $A Q=A R$ and $\angle A=60^{{}^{\circ}}\therefore \quad \angle A Q R=\angle A R Q=60^{{}^{\circ}}\therefore \quad r_{1}=r_{2}=30^{{}^{\circ}}$ Applying Snell's law on face $\mathrm{AB}$. $\begin{array}{l} \sin\mathrm{i}_{1}=\mu \sin \mathrm{r}_{1}$\\ \Rightarrow \sin $\mathrm{i}_{1}=\sqrt{3} \sin30^{{}^{\circ}}=\sqrt{3} \times \frac{1}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$\\ \therefore \quad $\mathrm{i}_{1}=60^{{}^{\circ}} \end{array} Similarly, \mathrm{i}_{2}=60^{{}^{\circ}}$ In a prism, deviation $\delta=\mathrm{i}_{1}+\mathrm{i}_{2}-\mathrm{A}=60^{{}^{\circ}}+60^{{}^{\circ}}-60^{{}^{\circ}}=60^{{}^{\circ}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If \(\varepsilon_0\) and \(\mu_0\) are the electric permittivity and magnetic permeability in vacuum, \(\varepsilon\) and \(\mu\) are corresponding quantities in medium, then refractive index of the medium is
questions.solution:
We know that velocity of electromagnetic wave in vacuum \(\left(\mathrm{v}_0\right)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}\) and velocity of electromagnetic wave in medium is
\(\text{(v) }=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu \varepsilon}} \text{. }\)
Therefore refractive index of the medium
\(\begin{aligned}
(\mu) & =\frac{\text{ Vel. of E.M. wave in vacuum }\left(\mathrm{v}_0\right)}{\text{ Vel. of E.M. wave in medium(v) }} \\
& =\frac{1 / \sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}{1 / \sqrt{\mu \varepsilon}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mu \varepsilon}{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}
\end{aligned}\)
